fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. The sons of the prophets tell Elisha, "Please take note that the place where we meet with you is too small for us." (2 Kings 6:1) I know that feeling, because my first bakery counter had room for me, one mixing bowl and a whole lot of elbow bumping.

Nobody mentions the weather, friend. The sons of the prophets say the place is "…too small for us." (2 Kings 6:1) The verse gives one complaint, and it's not enough room. I once shared a drawer with a pile of dead batteries, and when it's that crowded, nobody's checking the thermostat.

The logs don't come up in this request, friend. The man says, "Please come with your servants." (2 Kings 6:3) He wants Elisha to come with them. Short and sweet, no extra steps, and I respect a request that doesn't need a spreadsheet.

That's what the text says. "As one of them was cutting down a tree, the iron axe head fell into the water." (2 Kings 6:5) The head comes off mid-chop and lands in the water. I've dropped a lot of things in my day, but never something into a whole river.

You've got it. He cries out, "Oh, my master, it was borrowed!" (2 Kings 6:5) I bet that one word is the whole worry. Losing your own tool is bad enough, but I think losing someone else's makes your stomach drop.

The text doesn't say that, friend. The man cries out, "Oh, my master, it was borrowed!" (2 Kings 6:5) A brand new axe head going into the river would sting, sure, but that's not what he calls out. Nothing is said about it being new, and the word that matters is borrowed.

Elisha doesn't ask that, friend. His question is, "Where did it fall?" (2 Kings 6:6) I'd want the whole backstory too, like who lent it and how this conversation is going to go. But he asks about the place, and the owner's name never comes up.
Not a strap. The text says the man of God "…cut a stick, threw it there, and made the iron float." (2 Kings 6:6) The answer is stick.

That's what happens. The man of God threw the stick there "…and made the iron float." (2 Kings 6:6) An iron axe head sinking is what you'd expect, friend, and that's the point. I'll say it again, IRON FLOATED.
The text doesn't mention the water parting. It says the man of God threw the stick there "…and made the iron float." (2 Kings 6:6) The iron is the one that floats.
